title: Fast KVzip: Efficient and Accurate LLM Inference with Gated KV Eviction
claim: Our method matches the accuracy of the best compression baseline while cutting prefill time and memory well below both baseline and uncompressed inference.
layout: 2 side-by-side plots, left-to-right, shared colors for methods across panels
description: Two side-by-side plots with large serif titles, '(a) Performance' and '(b) Efficiency'. Panel (a) is a line chart. The x-axis is KV cache budget ratio from 0.2 to 1 and the y-axis is accuracy from 10 to 30 percent. Fast KVzip (red circles) and KVzip (green triangles) stay near 27 to 28 percent across budgets, while SnapKV (blue plus markers) falls steeply at low budgets. A boxed legend sits at the lower right. Panel (b) is a scatter plot of peak KV memory in GB (x-axis) against prefill time in seconds (y-axis), with dotted grid lines. Fast KVzip (red) is at the lower left, with low memory and low time. KVzip (green) is at the upper right with high time. No Compression (black) is at the right, with high memory and moderate time. The eye goes first to the red points, which are consistently best.
caption: Highlighted results. (a) KV cache compression performance on OpenAI MRCR [ref] compared to state-of-the-art methods using Qwen2.5-7b-1M [ref]. (b) Chunked-prefill efficiency for 170K tokens on Qwen2.5-7b-14M (BF16 precision) with 30% KV cache budget.
abstract: Efficient key-value (KV) cache management is crucial for the practical deployment of large language models (LLMs), yet existing compression techniques often incur a trade-off between performance degradation and computational overhead. We propose a novel gating-based KV cache eviction method for frozen-weight LLMs that achieves high compression ratios with negligible computational cost. Our approach introduces lightweight sink-attention gating modules to identify and retain critical KV pairs, and integrates seamlessly into both the prefill and decoding stages. The proposed gate training algorithm relies on forward passes of an LLM, avoiding expensive backpropagation, while achieving strong task generalization through a task-agnostic reconstruction objective. Extensive experiments across the Qwen2.5-1M, Qwen3, and Gemma3 families show that our method maintains near-lossless performance while evicting up to 70% of the KV cache. The results are consistent across a wide range of tasks, including long-context understanding, code comprehension, and mathematical reasoning, demonstrating the generality of our approach.
